doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: How Gibbs wrote songs
summary: Gibbs describes writing at the piano or in the car, storing eight-bar sketches and finishing them later.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you write songs sitting at the piano or did you —

I’ll tell you, I wrote both ways. Sometimes I’d sit down at the piano and I’d fool with different kind of chord changes, I would sing something and I’d write down the first eight bars. Other times I’d be in my car and I always carry paper, and I’d sing something and I thought it was pretty nice, I’d pull over and I’d write for eight bars. I’d take it over and I’d put it in my piano bench. And I’d do that a lot of times. And by the time I record next time I had about sixteen pieces of paper I put in there. I’d take them out and once when I played one I’d say, “What in the hell is this piece of garbage I was thinking about, it’s terrible.” And then, and that’s not bad. So then I would finish the song and write the next eight bars and provide a release. So I did it both ways.
